question: Does installing MATLAB still install Java?
answer:
Based on MATLAB R2026b [4]: No, starting in R2026b, MATLAB no longer includes Java as part of its installation on Windows and Linux; before R2026b, those installations did include Java Runtime [4][2].

To use Java, you need to install it after installing MATLAB. You can add the MATLAB Support for OpenJDK add-on or any compatible OpenJDK distribution [4]. MATLAB continues to support OpenJDK on all platforms [4]. R2026b also supports OpenJDK 25 Java from adoptium.net [4].

To install the add-on, click Add-Ons in the Environment section of the Home tab, search for OpenJDK in the Add-On Explorer, and install the MATLAB Support for OpenJDK add-on [2][7]. Then clear the current JRE in the Command Window with the following command so MATLAB uses the add-on [2]:

```matlab
jenv -clear
```

Calling `jenv` shows which Java version MATLAB currently uses on your system [7]. Also, in R2026b, the `"factory"` version argument for `jenv` and `matlab_jenv` is now the same as `"system"`, the default Java version on your system [4].

On Apple silicon Macs, the R2026b install steps still say to install a Java runtime yourself [5]. The sources don't say whether Mac installations ever included Java, since the release note refers only to Windows and Linux [4].

studyNotes.focus: Whether installing MATLAB in the current release (R2026b) still includes Java Runtime, or whether Java must be installed separately.

keyPoints.text: Starting in R2026b, MATLAB no longer includes Java Runtime as part of its installation on Windows and Linux.
Before R2026b, MATLAB installations on Windows and Linux included Java Runtime.
After installing MATLAB, users can install the MATLAB Support for OpenJDK add-on or any compatible OpenJDK distribution, and MATLAB continues to support OpenJDK on all platforms.
To use Java in MATLAB, a supported Java Runtime Environment must be installed on the system.

mayBeStale.text: Source 2 notes Oracle Java was included in a prior release and that a future release would stop including it; the R2026b notes confirm this change has taken effect.
Source 7 describes configuration steps and the jenv/matlab_jenv behavior for OpenJDK; these may change between releases, and the add-on install steps are specific to R2026b.
Source 6 is a search snippet about the R2026b prerelease system requirements and provides no Java-specific information.
